name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jeffries is a heavily funded incumbent House leader
Republican challenger has shown no fundraising or polling presence
Markets price Jeffries near certain to win
model.rationale: The district's D+24 lean, Jeffries' incumbency and roughly $15 million raised against an unknown Republican challenger with no visible resources all point to a lopsided race, and prediction markets price a Jeffries win at about 96%. The forecast stays at a Safe D with a margin near the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: A surprise red-wave national environment or an unexpectedly well-funded challenger could tighten the margin, though a seat this Democratic is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brooklyn-based NY-08 is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+24. Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, is running for another term and has raised nearly $15 million with $5 million on hand, while Republican Lewis Mizrahi reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Jeffries' chances at roughly 96 percent.

The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win for Jeffries, consistent with his prior margins in the district. The main uncertainty is simply how large the margin will be, not who wins, so the race carries wide but low-stakes uncertainty.
